description:
## Scope

Write the canonical 5-contract doc block on mail-server's
`create_object`, `update_object`, `destroy_object` foundation
methods (`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:59-134`). The
existing rustdoc already covers placeholder sentinels (create) and
Some/None semantics (update). Adds the remaining 4 contracts per
JMAP-x2gd.59:

1. **SetErrorType selection rules.** Which BackendSetError variant
   maps to which spec-mandated wire SetErrorType:
   - create_object: alreadyExists (for singleton TOCTOU),
     invalidProperties (for ill-shaped object), accountNotFound
     (when account_id is unknown).
   - update_object: notFound (id unknown), invalidProperties
     (server-set fields touched, immutable fields touched).
   - destroy_object: notFound (id unknown), forbidden (cascade-blocked,
     e.g. cannot destroy Mailbox containing emails when isPolicyDefault).
   - All three: BackendSetError::Other for storage-layer
     failures (mapped to wire `serverFail` by the handler).

2. **State-bump contract.** Every successful create/update/destroy
   call MUST bump the affected JmapObject type's state token so
   `Type/changes` subscribers see the mutation. The state bump and
   the storage mutation MUST be atomic with respect to other backend
   callers (reference impl uses one mutex acquisition; a database
   backend uses a single transaction).

3. **Cascade rules for destroy_object.** Define cross-type
   referential-integrity contract: when an Email is destroyed, what
   happens to the Mailboxes that referenced it via mailboxIds? When
   a Mailbox is destroyed, what happens to Emails whose mailboxIds
   contained it? Spec text (RFC 8621 §2 Mailbox/destroy) requires
   the backend to either reject (mailbox not empty) or cascade.

4. **Atomicity within multi-property updates.** A single update_object
   call MUST apply the patch all-or-nothing. A backend that
   partially-applies a patch and returns an error leaves the object
   in an undefined state; this is an implementation defect.

## Approach

For each of the three methods, add a sub-section with a heading
followed by the contract text. Use mail-specific examples
(Email/Mailbox/Identity/Submission) so the doc reads concretely.

Cross-references between methods are encouraged — the SetErrorType
table can live on create_object and be referenced from update/destroy.

## Verification

- `cargo doc -p jmap-mail-server` renders clean with -D warnings.
- `cargo test -p jmap-mail-server` passes (no behavior change).
- Read the existing reference impl in src/memory.rs once to confirm
  the contracts match actual behavior. Where they diverge, the
  doc states the contract and the impl is the bug (file a follow-up).

## Out of scope

Sibling propagation. Each sibling (chat, calendars, tasks, contacts,
filenode, metadata, sharing) has its own child bead under JMAP-x2gd.86
that picks up after this canonical doc lands.
title: Foundation methods doc sweep: write 5-contract block on mail-server canonical
